fit: freeze-dried cranberry powder and planned PHQ-9 in healthy older adults
assessment: Original COMBAT protocol schedules PHQ-9. The linked publication and complete supplement report cognition and other endpoints without a depression comparison. Confirmed same study family as ISRCTN76069316. Population and preparation differ from the frozen claim.

fit: ethanol ginger extract and acute exercise soreness
assessment: Table 3 means show lower pain after-exercise than before-exercise extract at 24 and 48 hours, reversing the abstract wording. Group-by-time p=.0001 does not identify each pairwise contrast. Dried-ginger extract and exercised healthy volunteers.

fit: steamed ethanol extract and postpartum perineal versus uterine pain
assessment: Perineal mean pain favored extract at three visits. Uterine group comparisons were inconclusive. Methods describe assignment by week and open design. No clinical Parkinson or grated ginger.

fit: standardized gingerol enriched extract and induced rat mechanical pain
assessment: Mechanical withdrawal thresholds favored treated injured animals. The data concern extract gavage and a laboratory nerve-injury endpoint.

fit: GGE03 and measured knee osteoarthritis pain
assessment: Publisher abstract reports favorable VAS and K-WOMAC with processed extract. Original numeric arm estimates and registration remain open.

fit: ginger supercritical extract and adult joint pain during exercise
assessment: The multivariate WOMAC group-by-time test gives p=.690. Selected items and within-arm changes do not establish a general between-arm pain effect. Registration followed study completion.

fit: GGE03 and separate abdominal-pain score in functional dyspepsia
assessment: GSRS abdominal pain change −5.0 extract versus −1.2 placebo (p<.001). SF-36 bodily pain also favored extract. This is the same cohort as the earlier local constipation record.

fit: standardized ginger extract granules and menstrual pain reporting discrepancy
assessment: The baseline statistics in Table 2 conflict with the displayed means and the prose. The original table gives no cycle-specific arm means. Official registry confirms design but gives no corrected estimate.

fit: Thirikadum product and menstrual pain with unresolved design
assessment: The original describes crossover and analyzes groups of 128 separately. The linked registry planned 378; the article reports 384. Exact contents and comparative estimate of a ginger-only intervention remain unresolved.

fit: supercritical ginger root extract and planned sciatica pain outcomes
assessment: Official registration and published protocol describe one sciatica trial with planned Brief Pain Inventory and McGill pain measures. No results posted and no grated exposure or Parkinson cohort.

fit: standardized ginger extract alongside ketoprofen in acute migraine
assessment: At 2 hours 56.7% versus 33.3% were pain-free (p=.03) with extract or placebo, both with ketoprofen. Study measures acute headache in a non-Parkinson population.

fit: standardized ginger extract and migraine prevention
assessment: At least 50% fewer attacks in 42% versus 39% after 90 days. Severe-pain days were also inconclusive. Different duration, extract and indication from the acute study.

fit: combined ginger and turmeric powder extracts and rat joint pain
assessment: The author abstract reports lower pain outcomes with a combined extract in an osteoarthritis model. The comparison does not isolate either plant.

fit: injected isolated curcumin and inflammatory nociception in mice
assessment: Later-phase formalin licking and separate writhing were reduced. Early-phase formalin findings were inconclusive. Injection, constituent and species differ from the frozen claim.

fit: isolated curcumin and tactile allodynia after laboratory nerve injury
assessment: The original body reports lower mechanical allodynia in animal oral and intrathecal curcumin comparisons. Whole culinary turmeric and clinical pain were not measured.

fit: combined ginger and turmeric powder extracts and rat joint pain
assessment: Reports attenuation in an animal osteoarthritis model after combined ginger and turmeric extract. Individual turmeric effect is unidentifiable.
